record_title: No even two-prime proper power-harmonic numbers
scientific_context: For every k>=2 there is no k-harmonic integer of the form 2^a p^b with a,b>=1 and p odd prime. Thus any even proper power-harmonic number must have at least three distinct prime factors. The proof uses incompatible primitive-divisor orders in the two geometric factors of sigma_k(2^a p^b).
limitations: The result does not exclude odd proper k-harmonic integers with exactly two distinct prime factors or even candidates with at least three distinct prime factors. Originality is to the best of our knowledge. The complete text of Cohen and Deng (1998), the primary source introducing k-harmonic numbers, was not directly accessible; a detailed standard handbook summary and bibliographic/citation records were checked, leaving residual coverage risk.

artifact_inventory.description: Standalone exact-integer verification over a finite grid of k, exponents, and odd primes.
Deterministic output of the finite verification: 42112 cases checked and zero hits.
